newsitem.title: USA: Dana to sell business to Mexico affiliate.
newsitem.headline: Dana to sell business to Mexico affiliate.

text.p: Dana Corp said Wednesday it planned to sell its transmission business to a unit of its Mexican affiliate, Spicer SA, as part of a plan to focus on its core businesses.
Dana, which makes vehicular products and systems, said in a statement it would sell the business to Spicer's Transmisiones TSP SA unit. Terms were not disclosed.

"This move is another element of our strategy of focusing on the company's core business units in order to meet or exceed corporate financial objectives by (January 1, 1999)," it said. "At the same time this move should further position Spicer SA with a very solid growth opportunity."
Dana holds a 49 percent share of Spicer, an affiliate since 1964. Unik, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Desc SA de CV, owns 51 percent.

Spicer operates vehicular component manufacturing and distribution facilities. Through Transmisiones, it has been manufacturing medium and heavy-duty transmissions for nearly 25 years and has supplied Dana with full transmission assemblies for more than 10 years.

Dana's transmission facilities in Knoxville, Tennessee, and Toledo, Ohio, will keep operating during the transition period, which is estimated to last a year. Dana is reviewing alternative uses of the Knoxville plant for other products.
